messages:
samir: Heads-up — proposal to avoid a huge console backfill by introducing a read-side projection (read-adapter) that maps the compact telemetry envelope into the current console analytics shape. thinking: shadow-write -> read-adapter -> gradual cutover.

alex: curious, can you sketch the adapter contract? what queries does the console really need vs raw events?

samir: good q. console mostly needs per-route/day aggregates, last-seen timestamps, and a handful of denormalized route metadata fields for the UI. not full event payloads. adapter would expose a small projection table and a compatibility API.

elaine: :+1: this would let Dedicated customers keep historic events untouched. but how do we ensure parity? we need evals comparing counts and top-k by route.

maria: two concerns: (1) index bloat if we create projection rows for every event, (2) write amplification during shadow-write. what's the expected RPS for projection route?

samir: answers: (1) we propose a coalesced projection keyed by (route_id, day) to store counters + last_seen + sample route_meta. reduces rows massively. (2) shadow-write overhead: +1 small writer per ingest partition — we measured ~8% CPU in a dev harness.

kofi: can you paste a tiny schema sketch?

samir: sure:

```sql
CREATE TABLE console_route_day (
  route_id text,
  day date,
  tokens_total bigint,
  requests_count bigint,
  last_seen timestamptz,
  sample_meta jsonb,
  PRIMARY KEY (route_id, day)
);
```

samir: adapter write will upsert increments + set last_seen if later, and update sample_meta via first_non_null merge. reads will be single-partition queries for console dashboards.

alex: sounds good. how will backfill work for historical data? full replay?

samir: plan: two-phase backfill — (A) streaming replay for last 90 days (fast path, incremental), (B) batch Spark job to process older buckets into the projection table with dedupe. avoid copying raw payloads.

maria: for (B) we need throttling and safety windows. also a feature-flagged console view so we can toggle between old and new projections during canary.

elaine: agree. also add monitors for shard imbalance and query latency. the console has tight SLAs for dashboard load.

kofi: what about cross-tenant queries and multi-tenant index sizing? do we partition by tenant + route?

samir: yes partition key = (tenant_id, route_id, day). that keeps per-tenant hot keys isolated. we'll add bloom filters for read-side to reduce scan cost.

devops-bot: deploy-plan-sanity-check: shadow-write enabled on ingest at 2:00 UTC, per-partition rollout, monitor cpu<30% and write-latency <50ms.

alex: can we avoid adding a new table by repurposing envelopev2? we already have an envelopev2 aggregation table but fields differ.

samir: envelopev2 currently stores raw compact attrs; it lacks denorm fields the console needs and its write pattern is append-only. projection gives us efficient upserts. repurposing would involve heavy schema churn and index rebuilds. I'd prefer projection.

maria: agreed. one more ask: include a sample SQL mapping snippet in the PR so reviewers can validate queries used by the console.

samir: will do. drafting a migration RFC with timelines: week1 shadow-write + small read-adapter atop new table, week2 canary console routes (5% users), week3 backfill rolling window for last 90d, week4 full cutover and deprecate old reads.

elaine: add a rollback runbook: stop shadow writes, switch console read to old table, drop projection after confirming no stale reads.

kofi: thumbs for RFC. also add storage cost estimate.

samir: will include cost + query perf numbers from dev harness. action items: samir -> RFC + SQL mapping, alex -> eval harness for parity tests, maria -> monitoring/playbook, kofi -> storage sizing. target RFC by EOW.

alex: acked.

maria: acked.

kofi: acked.
